note: Measured WCAG 2.2 AA conformance gaps that survive the browser matrix. An entry is a DEFECT, not a waiver: the library owes it. This file exists because no other generated artifact in the repository can express it -- `non-drag-alternative` in the capability matrix measures whether a KEYBOARD path is asserted, and a keyboard path satisfies SC 2.1.1, not SC 2.5.7, which requires a single pointer without dragging. A component can therefore read `non-drag-alternative: present` and still fail 2.5.7, which is exactly what happens to DzTable. Rendered by the docs site (TASK-N2-D2) on every affected component page and on /evidence/accessibility.

recordedAt.admissibility: locally qualified, worktree-dirty -- not release evidence

criterion.name: Dragging Movements
criterion.text: All functionality that uses a dragging movement for operation can be achieved by a single pointer without dragging, unless dragging is essential or the functionality is determined by the user agent and not modified by the author.

scope: Every component carrying the `drags` trait in packages/core/docs/quality-matrix.json. The trait names 9; all 9 were audited. The audited set is gated against the trait, so a tenth drag surface cannot appear without this file failing.
conformanceStatement: SC 2.5.7 AA is met for 6 of 9 drag surfaces. The three resize surfaces are keyboard-operable but require a drag for pointer operation.

surfaces.operation: reorder an item by dragging its grip
surfaces.keyboardAlternative: Space grabs the row, ArrowUp/ArrowDown move it, Space drops, Escape cancels and restores, Home/End move to the ends; each step announced in a live region.
surfaces.singlePointerNoDrag: Four always-visible controls -- move to top / up / down / bottom -- each a single tap.
surfaces.caveat: The single-pointer path is the move controls, rendered under `v-if="showControls"`. `showControls` defaults to true, so the component conforms as shipped; a consumer who sets `:show-controls="false"` and keeps the drag handle leaves reorder drag-only for a pointer user, and nothing warns them. The keyboard path survives that configuration; SC 2.5.7 does not.

surfaces.keyboardAlternative: Reka SliderImpl: arrows step, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End.
surfaces.singlePointerNoDrag: Reka emits slideStart on pointerdown anywhere on the track that is not a thumb, so one tap sets the value.

surfaces.keyboardAlternative: Reka SliderImpl: arrows step, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End.
surfaces.singlePointerNoDrag: Reka emits slideStart on pointerdown anywhere on the track that is not a thumb, so one tap sets the value.
handlePointerDown calls updateFromPointer(event) before any move, so a tap anywhere on the image moves the divider there.

surfaces.keyboardAlternative: Arrows step, PageUp/PageDown move one tenth of the range, Home/End.
surfaces.singlePointerNoDrag: handlePointerDown calls updateFromPointer(event) on the tap itself.

surfaces.keyboardAlternative: The drop zone is role="button" with tabindex 0; Enter and Space open the OS picker.
surfaces.singlePointerNoDrag: A plain click does the same. The drop path is an addition to the picker, never the only path.

surfaces.operation: drag the separator to resize panes
surfaces.gapReason: SplitterResizeHandle binds only onFocus/onBlur plus the pointer drag; there is no tap, no double-tap and no stepper control. Resizing by a single pointer requires a drag.
surfaces.ownerDecision: The affordance is a design decision with no APG precedent -- the Window Splitter pattern specifies keyboard interaction only, and APG has no column-resize pattern at all. Steppers, tap-to-place and preset cycling each change the component's visual language.
surfaces.notEssential: Dragging is not essential to resizing a pane: the keyboard path proves a non-drag mechanism exists, and the functionality is authored rather than user-agent-determined, so neither of the SC's own exceptions applies.

surfaces.operation: drag the separator to resize panes (DzSplitterHandle renders the same Reka SplitterResizeHandle)
surfaces.gapReason: The same shared Reka handle, so the same absence: focus and blur plus the pointer drag, and nothing else.
surfaces.ownerDecision: One implementation closes both DzResizable and DzSplitter.
surfaces.notEssential: Dragging is not essential to resizing a pane: the keyboard path proves a non-drag mechanism exists, and the functionality is authored rather than user-agent-determined, so neither of the SC's own exceptions applies.

surfaces.keyboardAlternative: onResizeKey on the focusable handle button: ArrowLeft/ArrowRight step 8px, 24px with Shift.
surfaces.gapReason: The handle responds to pointerdown plus pointermove only.
surfaces.ownerDecision: APG has no pattern for column resizing at all, so there is no precedent to follow.
surfaces.notEssential: Dragging is not essential to resizing a column: the keyboard path proves a non-drag mechanism exists, and the functionality is authored rather than user-agent-determined, so neither of the SC's own exceptions applies.

followUp: Add a single-pointer, non-drag path for two operations: (a) resize a splitter pane (DzResizable / DzSplitter, one shared Reka handle, so one implementation), and (b) resize a table column (DzTableCell). Each needs an affordance decision -- steppers, tap-to-place, or preset cycling -- and, if it is a rendered control, a data-part, an anatomy entry and a message id. Neither requires a public prop, and neither is a breaking change.
